newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to propose land policy changes.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to propose land policy changes.

text.p: An influential Japanese government panel on land policy will meet on November 21 to finalise proposals for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, a key member of the panel said on Wednesday.
The advisory panel, the Land Policy Council, is expected to make proposals to Hashimoto on changes to Japan's land policy the same day, Shozo Kono told reporters.
The panel would urge the government to take measures to seek the effective use of land instead of promoting land ownership, he said.
Land policy was last reviewed five years ago.
Since then, Japan has had a land policy aimed at curbing soaring land prices.
Kono said Japan's land prices had fallen to a point where the price surges in the latter half of the 1980s "bubble economy" had been offset after a five-year slump.
Soaring land prices during the bubble and falls afterward hit company balance sheets and resulted in massive problem loans for banks, he said.
"Emergency intervention measures are no longer needed to curb land prices," he said.
